A360 Media is a New York magazine and digital publisher, formerly American Media, known for celebrity journalism and health and fitness titles such as Us Weekly, Life & Style, OK!, Star, Men's Journal and Muscle & Fitness. It earns revenue from newsstand and subscription sales, advertising and licensing. It is backed by credit investors led by Chatham Asset Management, and a funding round of roughly $460M was recorded in January 2019. Consumer media brands with broad US recognition among celebrity and fitness readers, so audience reach is the main sponsorship value.

Aakash Educational Services is an Indian test preparation company based in New Delhi, offering classroom coaching, online courses and study material for medical (NEET) and engineering (JEE) entrance exams and school foundation courses. It sells to students and parents through a large network of coaching centres across India. It was acquired by Byju's in 2021 in a deal reported at about $1 billion. Strong education brand in India, with limited recognition outside the country; mainly relevant for youth and family audiences in India.

Arab African International Bank is a commercial and investment bank headquartered in Cairo, offering retail banking, credit cards, corporate lending, treasury and investment services. It was founded in 1964 as a joint venture owned by the governments of Egypt and Kuwait, and operates a branch network across Egypt. Customers include individuals, companies and institutions in Egypt. Recognised regional financial brand, mostly known within Egypt and the Gulf, with modest consumer awareness elsewhere.

Bank of Africa is a Moroccan banking group headquartered in Casablanca, also known as BMCE Bank of Africa. It provides retail, corporate and investment banking, with a large branch network in Morocco and subsidiaries in over 20 African countries, plus a European presence. It is part of the FinanceCom group controlled by the Benjelloun family and is listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange. Customers are individuals, small businesses and corporates. Well-known banking brand across Morocco and francophone Africa, and an existing sports sponsor in the region.

Binghatti is a Dubai property developer known for distinctive, design-led residential towers across Dubai, including projects branded with luxury partners such as Bugatti Residences, Jacob & Co and Mercedes-Benz Places. It sells apartments to local and international buyers and investors, and is a large builder of high-rise towers in the emirate. Founded by the Binghatti family and led by Muhammad Binghatti, it has raised debt in the form of sukuk bonds. Strongly branded, marketing-led developer in the UAE with visible billboards and sports and events sponsorship appetite.

Bridge Industrial is a Chicago real estate investment and development firm focused on industrial and logistics properties such as warehouses and distribution centres in major US markets. It acquires, builds and manages assets for institutional investors and tenants including e-commerce and logistics users, often through joint ventures. The Crunchbase data shows about $504M of funding, most recently in November 2025. Private B2B real estate firm with very little consumer brand visibility.

Century Communities is a US homebuilder based in Greenwood Village, Colorado, that builds and sells single-family homes and townhomes under the Century Communities and Century Complete brands, plus mortgage, title and insurance services through affiliates. It sells to first-time and move-up buyers across about 15 states and delivers several thousand homes a year. It is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker CCS). Consumer-facing homebuilder with local brand recognition in its markets, but limited national profile.

Employment Hero is a Sydney-based cloud HR, payroll and employee benefits platform for small and medium businesses. Its products cover HR management, payroll, recruitment, employee onboarding, learning, and benefits such as the Swag discount app and earned wage access. It was founded in 2014 by Ben Thompson, serves tens of thousands of businesses in Australia, New Zealand, the UK, Singapore and Malaysia, and became a unicorn after raising more than $500M in total funding. B2B software with growing employee-facing brand awareness; it has sponsored sport in Australia.

Epidemic Sound is a Stockholm music company that licenses a large catalogue of royalty-free music and sound effects to video creators, brands, broadcasters and agencies via a subscription model. Customers include YouTubers, podcasters, advertisers and media companies, who use the tracks without separate clearance. Founded in 2009 by Oscar Höglund and Ketil Kvalsund, it has raised over $500M and was valued at about $1.4B in 2021. Strong brand among creators and online video makers, known for creator sponsorships, though not a mainstream consumer name.

Ferrovial is a global infrastructure group, founded in Spain in 1952 and now domiciled in Amsterdam after relocating its legal seat in 2023. It builds and operates toll roads such as the 407 ETR in Toronto and managed lanes in Texas, develops airports including a stake in Heathrow, and runs construction and energy projects across North America and Europe. It is listed on Euronext Amsterdam, Madrid and Nasdaq (FER). Customers are governments and public agencies. A large corporate brand with moderate public awareness and prior sports and arts sponsorship.

FirstService Corporation is a Toronto-headquartered provider of property services in North America, split into FirstService Residential, the largest manager of residential communities, and FirstService Brands, which includes franchises such as Paul Davis Restoration, CertaPro Painters, California Closets, Century Fire Protection and Roofing. It serves homeowners associations, property owners and consumers and earns management fees and franchise revenue. It is listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (FSV) with revenue above US$4 billion. Many consumer-facing franchise brands, though the parent is little known publicly.

Forestar Group is a residential lot developer based in Arlington, Texas. It buys raw land and develops it into finished lots, which it sells primarily to homebuilders, with the majority going to D.R. Horton, which owns a controlling stake. Operating across roughly 20 US states, it has a lot pipeline of well over 100,000 lots. It is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker FOR). B2B land developer selling to builders, with very little consumer brand visibility.

Future Retail was an Indian retailer, the flagship listed company of Kishore Biyani's Future Group, operating Big Bazaar hypermarkets, Easyday supermarkets, FBB fashion stores and Foodhall. It served mass-market Indian shoppers through hundreds of stores. After a long dispute with Amazon and Reliance's attempted acquisition, it defaulted on debts and entered insolvency proceedings in 2022-23, with many stores closed or taken over. Once a household retail name in India but now largely defunct, so unlikely to be an active sponsor.

Global Telecom & Technology (GTT) is a US cloud networking provider based in Arlington, Virginia, selling managed SD-WAN, internet, wide-area networking, security and voice services to multinational enterprises and carriers over a global Tier 1 IP network. Its customers are businesses and government bodies in dozens of countries. It was listed on the NYSE under ticker GTT and grew through acquisitions, but filed for Chapter 11 in 2021 and was taken private by creditors. B2B telecom with minimal consumer awareness.

Highside Companies is a Denver real estate development and construction firm, built around its Highside Companies group that offers development, construction management and project management services. Its work includes multifamily and commercial buildings, often in Colorado and the western US. The Crunchbase entry shows about $500M of funding, most recently in August 2025. Privately held B2B business with local visibility in its home market and no consumer brand awareness. Further details on its scale are limited. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Homebound is a San Francisco company that builds custom homes for homeowners on their own lots, combining design, financing and construction in one service, aiming to simplify the build process through technology. It operates in selected US markets, mainly California and other fast-growing metro areas, and sells directly to consumers who own land or older homes to replace. Backed by venture investors, it has raised over $500M including debt, with its latest round in December 2025. Young direct-to-consumer homebuilding brand with regional awareness only.

Hyundai Glovis is the logistics arm of the Hyundai Motor Group, headquartered in Seoul, South Korea. It runs car-carrier shipping fleets, finished vehicle logistics, contract logistics, bulk shipping and Hyundai group parts distribution across several continents. Customers are mainly Hyundai, Kia and affiliates plus third-party shippers, with revenue above US$15 billion. It is listed on the Korea Exchange (086280), with Chung Eui-sun the controlling shareholder. B2B shipping brand with low consumer awareness, though known inside the automotive supply chain.

Idea Cellular was an Indian GSM mobile operator owned by the Aditya Birla Group, serving tens of millions of subscribers nationwide with voice, data and 4G services. It merged with Vodafone India in 2018 to create Vodafone Idea Limited, now branded Vi, one of India's three major private telecom operators, with the Aditya Birla Group and Vodafone Group as shareholders and the Indian government later becoming a significant shareholder. Vi is listed on the BSE and NSE. Consumer telecom brand with national visibility and a history of cricket sponsorship.

Incoco Capital is a New York real estate development and investment company focused on commercial and residential projects. The Crunchbase profile lists it under commercial real estate and records about $525M in funding, most recently in June 2025. Beyond that, public information on its portfolio, ownership and scale is limited, so the details here come mainly from the data supplied. It is a private B2B investor with no known consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Industrial Property Investment Fund (IPIF) is a London-based real estate fund, managed by Columbia Threadneedle Investments, that invests in UK industrial and logistics property such as warehouses and multi-let estates, with income distributed to institutional and pension investors. The Crunchbase entry classifies it under commercial real estate and leasing and shows about $400M of funding in June 2025. It is an investment vehicle rather than an operating brand, so consumer awareness is negligible and it is an unlikely sports sponsor.

InterRent REIT is a Canadian real estate investment trust based in Ottawa that owns, acquires and manages multi-residential apartment buildings in Ontario, Quebec and British Columbia, with a portfolio of roughly 15,000 suites. It earns rental income from residential tenants and aims to grow through acquisitions and renovations. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the ticker IIP.UN. Landlord brand with local consumer visibility among renters but no national sports presence.

Kunlun Core, spun out of Baidu's chip unit Kunlunxin and based in Haidian, Beijing, designs and manufactures AI accelerator chips and related hardware for AI infrastructure, targeting data centres, cloud providers and enterprises that train and run large AI models in China. Funding of about CN¥3.8 billion was recorded in December 2025, and it has been preparing for a stock market listing in Hong Kong. B2B semiconductor business with essentially no consumer brand awareness, though connected to Baidu.

Landing is a membership-based rental network based in Birmingham, Alabama, offering furnished apartments across the US that members can move between without new leases, so they can live flexibly in different cities. It targets remote workers, travellers and people in transition, charging a membership fee on top of rent. Founded around 2018, it has raised about $530M in equity and debt, with a round in May 2025. Direct-to-consumer brand with limited mainstream awareness.

Majid Al Futtaim Properties is the real estate arm of Majid Al Futtaim Holding, the Dubai conglomerate. It develops and operates Mall of the Emirates, City Centre malls across the Middle East and Africa, and community developments including Tilal Al Ghaf and Aljada, plus hotels and leisure venues such as Ski Dubai. Revenue comes from rent, hospitality and property sales, serving retail tenants and millions of shoppers annually. The group also runs Carrefour franchise stores across the region. High consumer visibility, frequent event sponsor in the UAE.

Mercon is a Coral Gables, Florida coffee company that sources, processes, trades and exports green coffee from Latin America to roasters and food companies worldwide, operating mills and warehouses across Central and South America. It also supplies coffee to major global brands. Privately held with a family-business heritage. Customers are roasters, food manufacturers and retail brands, and it earns money on trading margins and processing. B2B commodity supplier with almost no consumer brand awareness.

Ming Shing Group is a Hong Kong construction group, based in Kowloon City, offering civil engineering, foundation and site formation work and related building services, mainly as a contractor on public and private projects in Hong Kong. The Crunchbase entry records roughly $483M of funding, most recently in August 2025, and describes it as an engineering and construction firm. Limited public information is available beyond that, and it is a B2B contractor with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Moore Threads is a Beijing GPU developer founded in 2020 by former Nvidia China executive Zhang Jianzhong, designing graphics processors for AI computing, gaming and data centres, with its MUSA software platform. Customers are Chinese cloud and AI companies and PC users. It was added to US export restrictions in 2023 and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in December 2025 after raising roughly CN¥3.5B in a pre-IPO round. B2B chip firm with brand recognition mainly in China's technology and gaming circles.

Ole is a Toronto-based independent music publisher and rights manager that acquires and administers song catalogues, collecting royalties from streaming, radio, film and television use. Founded in 2004 by Robert Ott, it represents thousands of songs across genres. It is privately held, and the $500M funding figure reflects financing recorded in 2016. B2B music rights business with industry rather than consumer visibility.

Qutoutiao is a Shanghai mobile content app offering personalised news and short video, rewarding users with cash-style points for reading and referring friends, targeting lower-tier Chinese cities. It earns revenue mostly from advertising and from the Midu Novels reading app. It listed on Nasdaq in 2018 (QTT) and was later renamed Qtt Inc.. Large user numbers in China but low brand prestige, and it has little international profile.

Saudi Binladin Group is one of the largest construction contractors in Saudi Arabia, based in Jeddah, founded by Mohammed bin Laden in 1931. It has built major projects such as expansions of the Grand Mosque in Mecca, airports, highways and towers including the Abraj Al Bait. Customers are mainly government bodies. The group was heavily affected by a 2015 crane accident, and the government seized and restructured control in 2017. Large state-linked contractor with national recognition but no consumer marketing profile.

SM Investments Corporation is the Philippines' largest conglomerate holding company, based in Pasay City and controlled by the Sy family. Its businesses include SM Prime Holdings (malls and property), BDO Unibank, China Banking Corporation, SM Retail (department stores, supermarkets, SM Markets), and holdings in Atlas Mining and logistics. It is listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (SM) with a very large consumer footprint. Highly visible national consumer brand through SM malls and BDO, and an established sponsor of sports and events.

Spruce is a Houston, Texas finance company that provides consumer financing for residential solar systems, batteries and home energy upgrades, working through installers and solar sales channels. It offers loans and lease-style products to homeowners and has raised about $508M in funding, mostly debt facilities. It operates across the US. It is a niche B2B2C lender with little standalone consumer brand awareness and a modest marketing profile.

Steinhoff Asia Pacific is a Ryde, New South Wales business that was the Australian and New Zealand arm of Steinhoff International, the South African furniture and retail group. It owned household furniture retail and wholesale brands such as Freedom Furniture, Fantastic Furniture and Snooze before they were sold or restructured. Customers are Australian and New Zealand households through stores and online. Post the 2017 accounting scandal at the parent, assets were disposed and sold to Pepkor and others. Brands have consumer recognition in Australia.

TalonVest Capital is a Newport Beach, California boutique commercial real estate advisory and capital markets firm that arranges debt and equity financing and sells properties for owners, investors and developers across the US. Funding of about $483M was recorded in November 2025, which probably reflects a raise or a transaction recorded by Crunchbase. It is a private B2B firm with a small headcount and no consumer brand recognition. Limited further public information is available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Telefonica Germany is the German mobile and broadband operator, based in Munich, trading mainly as O2 and also running Alditalk and Blau as well as fixed broadband. Formerly E-Plus and O2 Germany, it serves about 45 million mobile connections, with revenue around EUR 8 billion. It is majority owned by Telefonica S.A. of Spain and is listed on the Frankfurt exchange (O2D), as O2 Telefonica. Strong consumer brand in Germany, a sponsor of events and sports, including football and the former Olympic Games.

Texas Pacific Land Corporation is a Dallas landowner holding about 880,000 acres in West Texas, mostly in the Permian Basin. It earns royalties from oil and gas production, and revenue from water sales and services, easements and land sales. It is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TPL) and has a very high market value for its size, with a lean team of employees. Customers are oil and gas operators. Limited consumer brand awareness; known mainly to investors.

The Honest Company is a Los Angeles consumer products company co-founded in 2011 by actress Jessica Alba, selling baby and personal care products including diapers, wipes, skincare and cleaning items, positioned as safe, plant-based and eco-friendly. It sells through retailers such as Target, Walmart and Amazon and online. It listed on Nasdaq in 2021 (HNST). Customers are consumers, especially new parents, mostly in the US. Recognisable consumer brand with celebrity-founder profile, strong with parents and moms.

Thor Industries is the world's largest recreational vehicle maker, based in Elkhart, Indiana, with brands such as Airstream, Jayco, Thor Motor Coach, Keystone, Heartland, Dutchmen and, in Europe, Erwin Hymer Group (Hymer, Eriba, Dethleffs). It sells through dealer networks to leisure and outdoor consumers, with annual revenue around US$10 billion. It is listed on the NYSE (THO). The Airstream and Jayco names have strong consumer recognition in North America and Europe, though the parent is less known.

Toll Brothers is a US luxury homebuilder based in Fort Washington, Pennsylvania, founded in 1967 by Bruce and Robert Toll. It designs, builds and sells single-family homes, townhomes and condos for move-up, empty-nester and luxury buyers, mostly in affluent suburban communities across many states, and also offers mortgage and apartment living. It is listed on the NYSE (TOL), delivering around 10,000 homes a year with revenue above US$10 billion. Well-known upscale brand in US housing, with local community marketing.

Two Roads Development is a West Palm Beach, Florida real estate developer focused on residential and mixed-use projects, with the Crunchbase profile showing about $520M of funding recorded in September 2025. Beyond its description as a property development company, there is limited public information available on its portfolio, owners and scale. It appears to be a private B2B developer with local visibility only and no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Urban Industrial is an Amsterdam real estate company that manages and develops logistics and industrial properties such as warehouses and last-mile distribution centres, serving logistics operators, e-commerce firms and manufacturers in the Netherlands and nearby European markets. The data supplied lists about EUR 470M of funding recorded in October 2025. Private B2B property business with no known consumer brand visibility, so sponsorship potential is low. Limited further information on ownership is available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

iFit is a Logan, Utah connected fitness company, formerly ICON Health & Fitness, that streams trainer-led workouts to NordicTrack, ProForm and Freemotion treadmills, bikes and rowers. It sells subscription programmes to home exercisers and equipment through retailers and direct. Revenue is largely subscription plus hardware, and it has raised more than $200M in funding, including a round led by Dick's Sporting Goods and others in 2019. Consumer fitness brand with national awareness in the US, and a natural fit for sport and health sponsorship.

APK2 is a Madrid-based parking management company that operates car parks and sells parking spaces, linked to real estate and rental assets in Spain. It manages garages in urban areas, serving drivers, residents and property owners, and has attracted about EUR 400M in funding recorded in January 2025. It appears linked to a private investment group in Spain. Limited public details are available on its portfolio size and ownership. B2B and local consumer service with little national brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Arcadia Group was a British fashion retail group headed by Sir Philip Green, owning high street chains Topshop, Topman, Dorothy Perkins, Burton, Miss Selfridge, Evans and Wallis, with stores across the UK and internationally. It collapsed into administration in November 2020 during the Covid crisis, and Asos bought Topshop and Topman, with Boohoo buying Dorothy Perkins, Burton and Wallis. Formerly a major British consumer brand with huge awareness, but defunct as a group, so not an active sponsor.

Black Banx is a Toronto-headquartered digital bank group offering online banking, multi-currency accounts, cards and crypto-related services to individuals and businesses, operating through licensed subsidiaries in several countries. Funding of about $382M was recorded in 2018. It has a global digital footprint but little verifiable public information on customer numbers, ownership or its regulation, so details should be checked. It has some online brand presence with no mainstream consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Bond Street REIT is a Charleston, South Carolina perpetual-life private NAV real estate investment trust, offering investors access to a diversified commercial property portfolio, such as industrial and other assets, through a non-traded structure. The Crunchbase record shows about $400M of funding in December 2025. It is a financial investment vehicle rather than an operating consumer business, with limited awareness beyond wealth advisers and investors. Sponsorship appetite is unlikely. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Bouygues Telecom is a French mobile, broadband and fixed-line operator based in Meudon, owned by the Bouygues group (about 90 percent). It serves roughly 25 million customers across consumer, business and wholesale segments, including the B&YOU low-cost brand, with annual revenue near EUR 6 billion. It acquired a stake in broadband business networks and operates fibre and 5G. Strong consumer brand across France and a long-standing sports and event sponsor, including football and rugby.

CargoX is a Sao Paulo, Brazil digital freight platform that connects shippers with truck drivers, handling road freight bookings, tracking and payments for cargo owners and independent carriers. It raised about $390M in funding, with its most recent round in November 2021, and has been through restructuring since then, with its business later merged or repositioned. B2B logistics technology brand known in Brazilian trucking and transport circles, with no consumer awareness.

d-Matrix is a Santa Clara, California AI chip startup building in-memory computing accelerators, such as its Corsair platform, designed to run generative AI inference efficiently in data centres. It sells to cloud providers and enterprises, and was founded in 2019 by Sid Sheth and Sudeep Bhoja. It has raised around $430M, including a funding round in November 2025, with investors including Temasek, Microsoft's M12 fund and Singapore-linked backers. B2B semiconductor business with no consumer brand visibility.

DVI is a Berlin-based real estate company, DVI Deutsche Vermögens- und Immobilienverwaltung, which buys, develops and manages residential and commercial properties in Germany and acts as a rental asset manager for institutional investors. The data shows about EUR 350M in funding recorded in May 2025. Beyond that, public details on its portfolio size are limited. It is a private B2B real estate firm, with little consumer brand visibility beyond tenants and property owners. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

EgyptAir is Egypt's state-owned flag carrier, based in Cairo, founded in 1932, and a member of Star Alliance since 2008. It flies to around 80 destinations across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and North America from Cairo hub, with a fleet of roughly 80 aircraft including Airbus A220s and Boeing 787s. Its cargo and maintenance divisions earn additional revenue. It carries millions of passengers a year and is owned by the Egyptian government. Strong national consumer brand and a history of sports sponsorship in Africa.

Emergent Cold is a Dallas-based temperature-controlled warehousing and logistics company. Funding of about $450M was recorded in 2021 to build cold storage facilities, mainly in North America and Latin America, serving food producers, grocers and distributors. It focuses on cold chain logistics for frozen and refrigerated goods. B2B infrastructure company with limited brand awareness outside food logistics, and low sponsorship likelihood. Further detail on its scale should be checked. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Five Point Holdings designs and develops large mixed-use, master-planned communities in California, including Newhall Ranch in Los Angeles County, Great Park Neighborhoods in Irvine and Candlestick Point and Hunters Point in San Francisco. It sells land lots to homebuilders and earns management fees. Based in Irvine, it is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (FPH) and in 2025 agreed to be acquired by Lennar-linked interests. Customers are builders and homebuyers. Little standalone consumer brand awareness, though the community brands are visible locally.

Flag Luxury Group and Unicorp National Developments are real estate partners, described in the data as working together on luxury residential development. Funding of about $386M is shown with a date in October 2026, which looks like a data entry artefact. No headquarters location is available in the input. Little else can be confirmed from the supplied information, and there is no known consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Flow is a Miami residential real estate firm, that develops lifestyle-oriented, branded apartment communities such as Flow House, along with hospitality-style amenities. The Crunchbase record shows about $450M of funding recorded in April 2025. It is a private developer and operator, with local brand presence in South Florida real estate but limited national awareness. Further details on its holdings and ownership are not confirmed from the data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Innovium was a Santa Clara, California fabless semiconductor company that developed TERALYNX Ethernet switching silicon for cloud data centres, selling to hyperscale cloud and networking equipment makers. Founded in 2014, it raised about $402M and was acquired by Marvell Technology in 2021 for around $1.1 billion in stock. Its technology now sits inside Marvell's data centre portfolio. B2B chip supplier with no consumer brand awareness and no standalone sponsorship profile.

Karpowership is a Dubai-registered operator of floating power plants, part of Turkey's Karadeniz Holding, run by the Karadeniz family. It owns the world's largest fleet of powerships, dozens of vessels, that moor offshore and sell electricity under long-term contracts to utilities and governments in countries including Lebanon, Ghana, Indonesia, Mozambique and Iraq, with supply of several thousand megawatts. Customers are state utilities. Controversial in some markets over contracts. B2B energy brand with limited consumer awareness.

Kontoor Brands is a Greensboro, North Carolina apparel company spun off from VF Corporation in 2019, owning the Wrangler and Lee denim and lifestyle brands, sold through department stores, mass retailers, Western wear shops and its own channels in the US, Europe and Asia. Revenue is around US$2.6 billion. It is listed on the NYSE (KTB). Wrangler is a long-standing rodeo and country music partner. Strong consumer brands recognised globally, and an established sponsor, notably of Professional Bull Riders and events.

LCI Industries is a supplier to the recreational vehicle and manufactured housing industries, headquartered in Elkhart, Indiana, listed on the NYSE (LCII). Its Lippert brand makes chassis, axles, slide-out systems, windows, doors, furniture, awnings and electronics for RV and trailer makers, with an aftermarket arm serving consumers and dealers. Major customers include Thor Industries and Forest River. Revenue is about US$3.8 billion. B2B brand with limited consumer recognition, though known in the RV community.

Lloyd's, or Lloyd's of London, is the world's specialist insurance and reinsurance marketplace based in London, where syndicates backed by capital providers underwrite risks including marine, aviation, energy, cyber and specialty lines. It is not a single insurer but a market of dozens of syndicates, and has operated for over 330 years, with annual premiums above GBP 50 billion. Customers are brokers and corporate clients worldwide. Regulated in the UK and well known as a financial institution, with a history of sponsorship, including sailing and racing.

Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited (MTNL) is an Indian state-owned telecom operator based in New Delhi, providing fixed-line, broadband and mobile services in Delhi and Mumbai, under the Ministry of Communications. It has been loss-making with heavy debt for years, and its government plans for revival include merging it with BSNL. It is listed on the BSE and NSE. Customers include consumers and businesses in the two metros. Known government telecom brand with declining market share and little marketing budget.

MCR Property Group is a Manchester, UK vertically integrated real estate firm that identifies, finances, develops and manages commercial and mixed-use property across northern England and the wider UK, including offices, industrial and residential schemes. It works with institutional investors and local authorities. Funding of about GBP 340M was recorded in October 2025. Founded by Manchester developers, it is privately held. Regional B2B brand with limited national consumer awareness.

Metrofibre Networx is a South African fibre network operator based in Centurion, Gauteng, building open-access fibre-to-the-home and business networks that internet service providers use to resell high-speed broadband to households and companies. It also provides carrier ethernet services, and has attracted large funding of around ZAR 6.5 billion, with investors including the Public Investment Corporation and Vodacom-related interests. Customers are ISPs, enterprises and consumers. B2B wholesale brand with moderate awareness in South African telecoms.

Transgaz, the Romanian national gas transmission system operator based in Medias (listed with Sibiu address), owns and operates Romania's high-pressure gas pipeline network and storage-related infrastructure, transporting gas to distribution firms and large industrial consumers. The Romanian state holds a majority stake, and shares trade on the Bucharest Stock Exchange (TGN). Funding shown reflects state-backed and bank financing of around RON 1.9B. Regulated infrastructure monopoly with little consumer marketing, though it sponsors some sports and community activities locally.

Sonos is a consumer audio company based in Santa Barbara, California, selling wireless multi-room speakers, soundbars, subwoofers, headphones such as Ace, and a music app that streams from services like Spotify and Apple Music. It sells through retailers and its own website in more than 50 countries, with revenue around US$1.5 billion. Founded in 2002, it listed on Nasdaq in 2018 (SONO). Strong premium consumer brand recognised globally, with a design-led image that suits partnership and entertainment tie-ins.

Tanger Med Port Authority manages the Tanger Med port complex in northern Morocco on the Strait of Gibraltar, one of Africa's and the Mediterranean's largest container ports, handling over 10 million TEU a year. The complex includes container terminals operated with APM Terminals and others, car, passenger and logistics zones. It is state-backed, working with industrial free zones hosting hundreds of companies. Customers are shipping lines and manufacturers, with government ownership. Infrastructure brand known in global shipping but low consumer awareness.

Thomas James Homes is an Aliso Viejo, California homebuilder that specialises in building new homes on infill lots in Southern California, Arizona and other markets. The data shows about $400M of funding in November 2025. It sells to home buyers and investors, with a focus on small infill communities. Regional builder with local brand awareness only, and uncertain scale. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Warehouse REIT was a London-listed real estate investment trust investing in UK urban warehouses and multi-let industrial estates, owning around 100 assets worth more than GBP 800M. It let space to small and mid-sized businesses and logistics firms. Managed by Tilstone Partners, it was listed on the London Stock Exchange (WHR), then received a takeover from Blackstone, agreed in 2025 and completed that year. Institutional property investment vehicle with no consumer brand profile.

Wessex Water is the regional water and sewerage utility for most of South West England, based in Bath, serving about 2.9 million customers in Somerset, Dorset, Bristol, Wiltshire and parts of Gloucestershire and Hampshire. It supplies drinking water and treats wastewater. It has been owned by Malaysia's YTL Corporation since 2002. Customers are households and businesses, and it is regulated by Ofwat. Regional household utility brand, sometimes attached to local sports partnerships, though water companies face reputational pressure over sewage discharges.

XCL Education is a Singapore-based education group operating international and private schools and related education services in Southeast Asia, including the XCL World Academy and other schools in markets such as Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam and Cambodia. Funding of about $400M was recorded in May 2025. It serves families seeking international curricula. Further details on enrolment, ownership and total school count were not confirmed from public information. Regional education brand with modest consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

YinLong Group, based in Zhuhai, Guangdong, manufactures and supplies lithium titanate batteries and energy storage systems for electric buses, commercial vehicles, rail and grid storage. Its Yinlong brand is known for fast-charging and long-life lithium titanate cells. Customers are bus makers, transit operators and energy companies, mainly in China, with exports to other markets. Funding of about $432M was recorded in 2016. B2B battery maker with little consumer awareness, though its products are visible on city buses. Limited detail on current ownership is confirmed.

Zhejiang Century Huatong Group, based in Shaoxing, Zhejiang, is a Chinese technology and gaming group, listed in Shenzhen (002602) under the name Century Huatong. It develops and publishes online and mobile games, including Legend of Mir related titles through its Shanda Games and Archosaur affiliates, and operates internet and cloud services. Customers are game players mainly in China and overseas. Funding of about $429M was recorded in 2021. Games publishers are known to Chinese gamers, but the corporate brand has low global awareness.

Banistmo is a Panama bank, headquartered in Panama City, providing retail, commercial and corporate banking, credit cards, mortgages and insurance products. It had raised about $584M and was acquired by TriNet in 2022, becoming TriNet Zenefits. Customers are small and medium-sized employers. Once a prominent start-up brand with big sponsorships and ads, it is now part of TriNet.

Assurant is a global provider of lifestyle and housing protection, based in Atlanta, Georgia and listed on the NYSE (AIZ). It sells extended warranties and device protection through partners such as mobile carriers and retailers, renters and lender-placed insurance, and vehicle service contracts, with revenue near US$11 billion. Customers are partners such as Apple, AT&T and Verizon and end consumers. Funding of about $469M was recorded in 2025. Strong B2B2C brand, but consumers often know it only through carrier insurance programmes.

Aurora Solar is a San Francisco software company whose cloud platform uses aerial imagery, 3D modelling and AI to design solar systems and generate proposals, used by installers and developers worldwide. Founded in 2013, it has raised about $523M, including a Series D in 2022, and has been used to design millions of projects. Customers are solar installers, utilities and sales teams. B2B SaaS brand highly known in solar and clean energy, with no consumer awareness.

Bank BTPN is an Indonesian bank based in Jakarta, known for serving micro-lending customers and pensioners through its Jenius digital banking app. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation became its majority owner, and in 2024 BTPN merged with SMBC Indonesia into one entity under the SMBC Indonesia name. Funding of about $500M was recorded in 2023. Customers include retail, SME and corporate clients. Jenius is a strong digital brand among younger Indonesians, with substantial marketing and some sports sponsorship.

Bulk Infrastructure Group is an Oslo-based infrastructure company that develops sustainable data centre campuses (including the N01 campus in Norway powered by hydroelectric energy), subsea fibre cable systems and related network infrastructure serving Nordic and international customers. Its projects are capital intensive and financed by investors. Funding of about $488M was recorded in 2026. B2B digital infrastructure operator with no consumer awareness.

Covalto is a Mexico City digital banking and services platform for small and medium businesses, formed from earlier lenders including Credijusto, and offering working capital loans, accounts and financial tools. It raised hundreds of millions of dollars in equity and debt, around $521M in total. Funding was recorded in 2022. It later faced financial problems, so its status should be checked. Customers are Mexican SMEs, and awareness is limited to the business lending market.

Deserve is a Palo Alto fintech that provides a mobile-first credit card platform, enabling partners to launch cards, including products aimed at students and people new to credit, with its own Deserve EDU Mastercard. Founded in 2013, it raised about $544M, including debt facilities, and has global partnerships including Mastercard. Customers are consumers building credit and business partners. Moderate brand awareness among young adults and students, but not a mainstream household name.

Hotel Equities is an Alpharetta, Georgia hotel management and development company, which operates hundreds of hotels under Marriott, Hilton, IHG and other brands in the US, covering select-service and extended-stay hotels. It also invests in and develops properties for institutional partners. Funding of about $500M was recorded in 2018. Customers are travellers using branded hotels, and owner clients. B2B hospitality operator that is not visible to consumers under its own name.

Jolywood is a Chinese photovoltaic materials and cell manufacturer, with its base in Changshu, Jiangsu, making solar backsheets, N-type TOPCon solar cells and modules for installers and solar developers. It is listed on the Shenzhen exchange and has expanded into cells and modules. Funding of about CN¥3.2 billion was recorded in 2022. Customers are solar module makers and project developers worldwide. B2B energy manufacturer, with little consumer brand awareness outside the solar industry.

MedcoEnergi is an Indonesian energy and natural resources company based in Jakarta, listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (MEDC). It explores and produces oil and gas in Indonesia, Oman, Vietnam and elsewhere, operates power generation including renewables, and has a stake in the Batu Hijau copper mine through Amman Mineral. Founded in 1980 by Arifin Panigoro, it is led by the Panigoro and Soeryadjaya families. Funding of about $500M was recorded in 2023. B2B energy brand with moderate visibility in Indonesia.

Ningbo Shanshan is a Chinese company, based in Ningbo, Zhejiang, listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600884), that makes lithium-ion battery anode materials, electrolytes and LCD polarizer films, plus past apparel interests. It supplies battery makers, with large customers in China's electric vehicle supply chain, and display manufacturers. Funding of about CN¥3.1 billion was recorded in 2022. B2B materials supplier with no consumer brand awareness, though it is a large name in battery materials.

Pele Green Energy is a Johannesburg independent power producer that develops, owns and operates solar and wind projects in South Africa, selling electricity to the grid and to commercial and industrial customers. The data shows funding of about R2.5 billion recorded in 2023. Customers are Eskom, municipalities and private energy buyers. Details on its capacity, shareholders and operating projects should be confirmed. B2B energy producer with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Petroleum Geo-Services (PGS) was an Oslo marine seismic company that acquired subsea seismic data using survey vessels and sold it to oil and gas companies, and listed on Oslo Bors (PGS). It merged with TGS in 2024 in an all-share deal, creating a larger energy data and seismic group. Customers were energy exploration firms. Funding of about $491M was recorded in 2023. B2B energy services brand with no consumer awareness, and now part of TGS.

Priority Power Management is a Texas energy management and consulting firm, listed in the data at Arlington, helping large commercial and industrial customers buy electricity and natural gas, manage costs, and handle demand response and energy procurement. The Crunchbase entry records about $500M of funding in 2022, which likely includes a significant investment. Customers are businesses and oilfield operators. B2B consultant with little consumer visibility. Further details of its ownership and size should be confirmed.

Promasidor is an African food manufacturer that produces and sells dairy powders and seasonings under brands such as Cowbell milk, Onga seasonings, Loya milk and Miksi, sold across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and about 20 other African countries. Founded in 1979 and listed in the data at Lagos, it is privately owned, with group origins in Johannesburg. Funding of about $532M was recorded in 2016. Strong mass-market consumer brands in West Africa and a regular sports and school sponsor.

SeatGeek is a New York ticketing company with a mobile-first marketplace for primary and resale tickets to sports, concerts and theatre, with technology partnerships with teams and venues, including NFL teams and major arenas. Founded in 2009 by Jack Groetzinger and Russ D'Souza, it has raised about $510M and is a challenger to Ticketmaster. It earns fees from ticket sales. Strong consumer brand among US live-event fans, with heavy sports and entertainment marketing.

Shadowbox Studios is a Los Angeles company that operates a large independent film and television studio campus, with its main facility in Georgia, offering soundstages, backlots and production support to studios and streaming productions. It is backed by private capital, with about $500M of funding recorded in 2022 to build and expand studio space. Customers are film and television producers. B2B entertainment infrastructure with no consumer awareness. Details on locations and ownership should be confirmed.

Skeleton Technologies is an Estonian-founded maker of ultracapacitors and energy storage technology, headquartered in Tallinn, with its main factory in Markranstadt near Leipzig, Germany. Its high-power ultracapacitors and curved graphene-based SuperBattery are used in transport, grid stability, industry and defence, and it was founded in 2009 by Taavi Madiberk. It has raised about $490M. Customers include automakers, rail and wind companies. B2B technology brand with little consumer awareness.

Swedish Logistic Property (SLP) is a Malmo-based Swedish company that develops, owns and manages modern, energy-efficient logistics properties such as warehouses and distribution centres in Swedish growth regions, for tenants including retailers and logistics companies. It has been listed on Nasdaq First North and Stockholm markets, with funding of about SEK 5.4 billion recorded in 2026. B2B property investor with low consumer awareness and a small number of employees. Details of listing venue should be confirmed.

Zakher Marine International is an Abu Dhabi-based marine and offshore oil and gas services company that operates vessels supporting the energy industry in the Gulf region and beyond. The data records about $500M of funding in 2022, which probably includes financing for fleet expansion. Customers are national oil companies and offshore operators. Detailed information on fleet size, ownership and contracts could not be confirmed. B2B maritime business with no consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Branch is a Mountain View, California financial technology company that offers businesses tools for fast, flexible pay options for hourly workers, including instant wage access and digital payments through a Branch wallet and card. The data records about $667M of funding in 2022, including debt facilities. Customers are employers and their hourly employees, particularly in retail, hospitality and logistics. Not to be confused with Branch Metrics, the mobile linking software. Moderate B2B2C brand awareness in the US.

AGBO is a Los Angeles film and television studio founded by directors Anthony and Joe Russo, behind the Avengers films and Cherry, and the producer of series such as Citadel for Amazon and films like Everything Everywhere All at Once. It develops intellectual property universes for film, TV and games, and has raised about $400M in 2022, including a major investment from Apollo funds. Customers are streaming platforms and studios. High name recognition in film circles, and a creative brand attractive to entertainment partners.

AmeriLife is a Clearwater, Florida insurance and retirement solutions distributor focused on seniors, selling Medicare Advantage, life, annuity and health products through agents, brokerages and marketing organisations across the US. It has grown rapidly through acquisitions of agencies, and is backed by Genstar Capital and Thoma Bravo. Funding of about $395M was recorded in 2022. Customers are older Americans and independent agents. Consumer-facing in senior insurance markets, although mostly through local agency brands, and it has used sports sponsorship.

Azrieli Group is an Israeli real estate and infrastructure group based in Tel Aviv, listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (AZRG), founded by David Azrieli. It owns Azrieli Malls, office towers including the Azrieli Center in Tel Aviv, and Sarona, hosts data centres through Green Mountain, and has interests in renewable energy. Funding of about 1.4B was recorded in 2026, likely bonds. Strong landmark brand in Israel, with malls visited by millions of shoppers.

Beazley is a London specialist insurer operating at Lloyd's, listed on the London Stock Exchange (BEZ). It underwrites cyber, marine, political risk, property, specialty and reinsurance for businesses and professionals in the UK, US and worldwide, with premiums above US$6 billion. It is a leader in cyber insurance. Funding of about 350M was recorded in 2022 as a capital raise. Customers are brokers and corporates. B2B insurer with strong reputation in the insurance market but little consumer awareness.

Cinesite is a London visual effects and animation studio, founded in 1991 as a Kodak operation and now independent, providing VFX for films such as Harry Potter, James Bond and Marvel productions and producing animated features. It has studios in London, Montreal, Vancouver, Berlin and Mumbai. Funding of about $418M was recorded in 2022, and investor details should be confirmed. B2B studio known in the film industry, with little consumer brand awareness.

EcoPro BM is a South Korean maker of cathode active materials and precursors for lithium-ion batteries, based in Cheongju, Chungcheongbuk-do and listed on KOSDAQ (247540). It sells nickel-rich NCA and NCM cathodes to battery makers such as Samsung SDI and SK On, supplying electric vehicle makers, and has plants in Korea, Hungary and Indonesia. It is part of the EcoPro Group. Funding of about $385M was recorded in 2023. B2B materials supplier with no consumer awareness.

Engie Energia Chile is a Chilean electricity generator and transmission company, based in Las Condes, Santiago, controlled by the French Engie group and listed on the Santiago Stock Exchange (ECL). It operates coal, gas, solar, wind and storage plants, and supplies power to mining companies, industries and distributors in northern and central Chile. It is also moving away from coal. Funding of about $400M was recorded in 2023. B2B energy provider with modest consumer recognition.

Entra is a Norwegian real estate company, based in Oslo and listed on Oslo Bors (ENTRA), that owns, develops and manages office buildings, mostly in Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim and other larger Norwegian cities, with a strong sustainability focus. Its tenants include public sector bodies and companies. The Norwegian state used to hold a major stake. Funding of about NOK 4.1 billion was recorded in 2026. B2B property company known in Norway's business community, with low consumer visibility.

Holly Energy Partners was a Dallas master limited partnership, listed on the NYSE (HEP), that owned pipelines, terminals, tankage and loading racks serving HollyFrontier and other refiners in the Southwest and Rocky Mountain regions. HF Sinclair, the refiner and sponsor, bought out the public units in December 2023, taking it private. Customers were refineries and oil producers. Funding of about $400M was recorded in 2022. B2B midstream asset with no consumer awareness and no standalone existence now.

Inspiration Mobility is a Washington, DC company that offers EV solutions for ride-hail and gig drivers, combining vehicle leasing and rental, charging access, maintenance and financing in markets such as California, so drivers can electrify more affordably. It has raised about $415M in equity and debt, recorded in 2022. Customers are rideshare, delivery and fleet drivers. Niche mobility brand with local awareness among drivers.

Ivi is a Russian online video-on-demand platform based in Moscow, offering films, TV series and original content on a subscription and ad-supported basis to tens of millions of monthly users in Russia and CIS. Founded in 2010, it has raised about $435M, and is among the largest Russian streaming services. Funding was recorded in 2021. Customers are viewers and advertisers. Strong consumer brand in Russia, though sanctions and market conditions limit Western partnerships.

Lucero Energy is described as an oil company focused on the acquisition and development of oil and gas assets, located in Denver, Colorado, with about $442M of funding recorded in 2022 according to Crunchbase. Several similarly named companies exist, including a Canadian company, so the exact entity is unclear. Its fields, production, ownership and customers cannot be confirmed from the data. B2B energy producer with no consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

SITA is a Geneva-based IT and communications provider for the air transport industry, owned by its members, which include airlines, airports and other aviation bodies. It supplies airport check-in and baggage systems, passenger processing, border management, aircraft communications and data networks, serving most of the world's airlines and airports. Founded in 1949, it has annual revenue near US$2B. Funding of about $400M was recorded in 2022. B2B aviation technology brand with little awareness among travellers.

Societe nationale industrielle et miniere (SNIM) is Mauritania's state-owned mining company, with operations in iron ore around Zouerate and rail and port facilities in Nouadhibou, the country's key export route. It is the nation's largest industrial employer and a main source of foreign exchange, shipping iron ore concentrate mainly to Europe and Asia. Funding of about $425M was recorded in 2025, likely for expansion. B2B state enterprise with strong national profile in Mauritania but little consumer-facing activity.

SolarSpace is a Chinese solar company based in Xuzhou, Jiangsu, engaged in developing, producing and selling solar cells, including high-efficiency N-type cells, and modules for solar developers and installers. The Crunchbase entry records about CN¥3.0 billion of funding in 2022. The company is part of the fast-growing Chinese solar manufacturing sector. Customers are module makers and project developers worldwide. B2B energy equipment maker with no consumer awareness. Ownership and listing should be confirmed.

Virescent Renewable Energy Trust is an Indian infrastructure investment trust (InvIT) focused on solar power, based in Mumbai and sponsored by KKR-backed Virescent Infrastructure. It owns operating solar projects selling electricity to state utilities and corporates, with the objective of generating income for unit holders. Funding of about INR 32.6 billion was recorded in 2022. Customers are distribution companies and industrial power buyers. Investment vehicle with no consumer brand profile, so sponsorship is unlikely.
